question.problem: Consider the vector $u=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ \sqrt{k} \\ -\sqrt{k} \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Given that $u\cdot v=-2$ and $‖v‖=1$, what is the smallest possible value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,

$$
|u\cdot v|\le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖.
$$

We are given all the quantities in the inequality above, except for $‖u‖.$ So first, we compute $‖u‖$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(\sqrt{k})^{2}+(-\sqrt{k})^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2+2k}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|u\cdot v| & \le ‖u‖\cdot ‖v‖ \\ |-2| & \le \sqrt{2+2k}\cdot (1) \\ 2 & \le \sqrt{2+2k} \\ {2}^{2} & \le {(\sqrt{2+2k})}^{2} \\ 4 & \le 2+2k \\ 2 & \le 2k \\ k & \ge 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $k$ is $1.$
